documents.title: Researchers Develop Longer-Lasting Battery
documents.text: CAMBRIDGE (September 14) - A team at Wexford University has developed a battery that can be charged in ten minutes and lasts twice as long as the lithium-ion models used in most smartphones. [A] The breakthrough, led by materials scientist Dr. Hui Zhang, relies on a new silicon-based material that stores more energy without overheating. [B] In laboratory tests, the prototype kept 90 percent of its capacity after 1,500 charging cycles. [C] The research was funded by the national science council and the electronics company Delta Devices, which holds an exclusive license to use the technology in consumer products. [D] Commercial batteries based on the design are not expected before 2028, as the manufacturing process must first be made cheaper and easier to scale.

questions.prompt: What does the article describe?
questions.explanation: The article reports on a battery developed at Wexford University.

questions.prompt: What is NOT true about the new battery?
choices: It charges in about ten minutes
It kept most of its capacity in tests
It is already sold in stores
questions.explanation: Commercial batteries are not expected before 2028.

questions.prompt: In the last sentence, the word "scale" is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Making a process easier to scale means making it easier to expand to large production.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "Most current batteries start to lose capacity after about 500 cycles."
questions.explanation: It compares with the 1,500 charging cycles reported in the laboratory tests just before [C].

documents.title: Summer dress code
documents.text:
TO: All employees
FROM: Human Resources
DATE: May 15
SUBJECT: Summer dress code

Starting June 1, we will relax our dress code for the summer months. From June through August, business casual attire is acceptable every day, and on Fridays employees may wear jeans and company T-shirts. Open-toed shoes are permitted, except in the laboratory and on the production floor, where closed shoes are mandatory for safety reasons. Employees who meet with clients are still expected to dress formally on the day of the meeting. Shorts, tank tops, and flip-flops remain unacceptable. We appreciate your cooperation in maintaining a professional image.

documents.title: Public Hearing Notice
documents.text: The Fairmont Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on Thursday, November 14, at 7 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber to consider a proposal to rezone the property at 900 Quarry Road from industrial to mixed residential and commercial use. The developer, Cobalt Properties, plans to build 240 apartments, a small grocery store, and a public park. Residents may speak for up to three minutes each; those wishing to speak must sign up at the door beginning at 6:30 p.m. Written comments may be submitted by e-mail to planning@fairmont.example until November 12 at 5 p.m. The meeting will also be streamed live on the city website. No vote will be taken at this meeting; the commission will decide on December 5.

A hearing on changing how land may be used

documents.text: Join us on Friday, September 6, from 6 to 9 p.m. for the opening of Lumen Gallery's first exhibition, "Light and Landscape," featuring 40 paintings and photographs by regional artists. Nina [7:17 p.m.]: Can you book a table for four at 8?

documents.title: Kessler Foundation Scholarship
documents.text:
Eligibility: Applicants must be high school seniors with a minimum 3.5 GPA, live in Brent County, and plan to study engineering, nursing, or education.
Award: $4,000 per year for up to four years.
Required documents: transcript, two letters of recommendation, a 500-word essay, and proof of residence.
Deadline: March 1 (postmark). Finalists will be interviewed in April; winners are announced on May 15. The scholarship is renewable if the student maintains a 3.0 GPA.

documents.title: Scholarship application
documents.text:
Dear Kessler Foundation,
I am a senior at Pinewood High School and wish to apply for your scholarship. I plan to study nursing, and I currently have a 3.7 GPA. I live in Brent County. I have already gathered my transcript and one letter of recommendation from my chemistry teacher. A second letter, from my volunteer supervisor at Mercy Hospital, will arrive by February 20. My family recently moved to a rental apartment, and I do not yet have a utility bill in my name. May I use my lease as proof of residence? I am enclosing my essay, which is 520 words. I hope that is acceptable.
Respectfully,
Amelia Torres

documents.title: Valley Growers Co-op to Open Retail Store
documents.text: FAIRVIEW (March 11) - Valley Growers Cooperative, owned by 85 local farms, will open its first retail store on Mill Street on April 5. The 4,000-square-foot store will sell fresh produce, dairy, honey, and baked goods, all sourced within 50 miles. "Customers want to know where their food comes from," said manager Carla Esposito. Prices will be similar to those of supermarkets, and members of the co-op receive a 10 percent discount. The store will be open Tuesday through Sunday and will offer free cooking demonstrations on Saturday mornings.

I read about your new store. I own Maple Bistro and buy produce for about 120 meals a day. Do you offer wholesale prices for restaurants? I would especially like to order tomatoes, herbs, and eggs. Also, could you deliver on Mondays, when your store is closed?
Henry Ito

documents.title: Valley Growers Wholesale Program
documents.text: Restaurants and caterers can order directly from our farms at wholesale prices, 15 percent below retail. Minimum weekly order: $200. Orders must be placed by Thursday for delivery the following Tuesday or Wednesday. Payment terms: net 30 days. To apply, send a copy of your business license to wholesale@valleygrowers.example.
